findings.text:
- [P2] Match import routes to the mounted blob before suppressing aliases — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/rust_reverse_gap_candidates.sql:61-65
  When a file is mounted with unsaved overlay content, its placement still points to the persisted summary member, but `import_id` and `route_ordinal` belong to the mounted blob and can be reused for a different import. This join can therefore mistake a persisted resolved route for the overlay's unresolved import and suppress its alias from the name closure, causing reverse-reference discovery or completion to miss gaps. The same issue affects the other alias-closure branches using this join.

- [P2] Do not match persisted import identities against an edited mount — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/rust_reverse_gap_candidates.sql:61-65. When a file has an unsaved or otherwise changed mounted blob, `placement.summary_id` and `member_ordinal` refer to the persisted blob, while `imported` belongs to the mounted blob. Import IDs and route ordinals are blob-local, so an unrelated persisted resolved import can coincidentally match an unresolved import in the edited file. This suppresses the alias from the name closure and can omit reverse-reference candidates and completeness gaps. The same comparison occurs in the other alias branches.

- [P2] Match import routes only against their persisted blob: crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/rust_reverse_gap_candidates.sql:64-65. When a mounted file has unsaved changes, `imported` describes the mounted blob while the summary route and its import IDs and ordinals describe `placement.placement_blob`. These blob-local IDs can coincide after an edit even when they refer to different imports, so an unrelated persisted route can suppress an unresolved alias from the name closure, causing reverse-reference candidates and completeness gaps to be missed. The previous join required the route's blob to equal `imported.blob_id`; the same issue affects the other three replacement joins.

- [P2] Do not match overlay import ordinals against the base summary — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/rust_reverse_gap_candidates.sql:61-65. When an edited overlay changes an import, the placement still points to the saved file's summary, while `imported.source_import_id` and `imported.ordinal` belong to the overlay blob. Those blob-local numbers can coincide with a different, previously resolved import in the saved file, causing this `NOT EXISTS` to suppress the overlay's unresolved alias and omit its reverse-gap candidates. The previous join also required the bound import's blob to equal the overlay blob; the same issue affects the other changed route checks.

- [P2] Look up earlier imports in enclosing scopes — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:559-561
  When an import is declared inside an object or method and its head was imported in an enclosing scope, such as `import io.k.XMLUtils; object Use { import XMLUtils.Escapes }`, the lookup uses only the inner `source_scope_head` and cannot find the visible outer import. The resulting route is unresolved even though Scala lexical scope makes the earlier import available.

- [P2] Do not skip unresolved segments of a relative import path — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:631-635. For a Scala file in package `app`, `import foo.Obj.Bar` tries `app.foo.Obj` and then `app.foo` as packages, but the latter lookup searches directly for `Bar` and ignores `Obj`. If `app.foo.Bar` exists, it can be bound to this import and prevent the actual `foo.Obj.Bar` route from being considered. Only a package prefix that accounts for the entire owner route can directly provide the imported member; shorter prefixes need member traversal.

- [P1] Require the package prefix to consume the import route — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:632-647
  When a Scala file in `app` imports `Picklers.Tag` and both `app.Tag` and `app.Picklers.Tag` exist, the relative route eventually queries package `app` for `Tag`, creates a bridge to the unrelated top-level class, and skips the member-owner lookup. A package candidate must not satisfy an import while `Picklers` remains unconsumed in the route.

- [P2] Search enclosing scopes for earlier Scala imports — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:559-561. When an earlier import is in an enclosing scope, such as `import io.k.XMLUtils` at file scope followed by `object Use { import XMLUtils.Escapes.unescMap }`, the two imports have different scope heads, so this lookup cannot find the already resolved `XMLUtils` route. The nested import consequently fails even though the earlier import is visible there; the route lookup needs to follow lexical scope ancestry.

- [P2] Mark successful relative package imports as having an owner — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:865-867
  When a Scala file in `app` imports `sub.Foo` and `Foo` is declared directly in package `app.sub`, the relative route produces a package bridge and exits here, but `package_prefix_found` remains false because it is only set for non-relative package routes or member continuations. The subsequent owner-open gap therefore marks this successfully resolved import incomplete, affecting every lookup that uses it.

- [P2] Resolve earlier imports from enclosing scopes — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:559-561: When an import inside an object or method uses a name imported at file scope, such as `import io.k.XMLUtils; object Use { import XMLUtils.Escapes.unescMap }`, the two imports have different scope heads, so this lookup cannot find the visible earlier import. Consequently the newly added route composition fails for ordinary nested scopes even though Scala makes the outer import visible there.

- [P2] Order imports by source position — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:417-419
  For multiple imports in one file, `token.ordinal()` is the mount ordinal and is identical for every token, so this sort preserves the candidate reader's order rather than source order. The earlier-import map can consequently miss a preceding import or make a later import visible to an earlier one, depending on candidate enumeration order.

- [P2] Order earlier imports by source position — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:417-420: For multiple imports in the same Scala file, `token.ordinal()` is the mount ordinal, so every local token has the same sort key. The loop therefore processes imports in the inventory's candidate order rather than source order, allowing a later import to be used as an earlier one or preventing a valid earlier import from being available when a dependent import is processed. Sort by the import's actual source position before building `earlier_scala_imports`.

- [P1] Require the entire package route before selecting a package member — crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs:631-648
  When a Scala file in `package app` imports `io.k.Widget` and `app.Widget` also exists, the new relative route `app.io.k` falls back to the existing `app` package and selects its `Widget`, even though `io.k` was never resolved. That bridge makes the loop stop before trying the actual `io.k` route, so the import resolves to the wrong declaration. Only a package matching the complete owner route should supply a direct package member; shorter prefixes need member continuation instead.
